news.title: UK house prices fall 0.4% in August 2026: Lloyds data
news.para: In August, British house prices experienced their first yearly decline in nearly three years, driven by higher borrowing costs that dissuaded potential buyers. Economists predict continued softness in the housing market as uncertainty from global events looms, especially after official data revealed a decrease in annual price growth leading up to June.

news.title: Chandigarh estate office simplifies property services, drops separate NDC requirement
news.para: The Chandigarh estate office has done away with the No Dues Certificate, enhancing the efficiency of property service applications. Now, all government dues verification will occur in a single step, resulting in one demand notice for any outstanding fees. This change not only cuts down on paperwork but also promises to process complete applications within just fifteen working days.

news.title: Arnya RealEstates launches ₹750 crore AIF with Casagrand
news.para: Arnya RealEstates Fund Advisors has launched Arnya Real Estate Fund III – Preferred Capital, a Category-II AIF with a target corpus of ₹750 crore. The fund, launched in partnership with Casagrand Premier Builder, will invest in residential projects across Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

news.title: Are our cities still being planned for a climate that no longer exists?
news.para: Urban planning needs to evolve alongside climate change, leaving outdated historical data behind. Infrastructure built for previous weather patterns may falter against the extreme conditions of the future. Urban areas play a pivotal role in shaping local climates. As India urbanizes swiftly, it is crucial to implement development strategies that withstand future climate projections, ultimately paving the way for resilient urban environments.

news.title: Cabinet nod for Greater Noida West metro likely this month
news.para: The Greater Noida West metro project awaits Union Cabinet approval this month.  This crucial step will enable tendering and construction of the new corridor.  The proposed 8.4km elevated line will connect Noida Sector 51 to Greater Noida West.  Five stations will serve residents, easing current commuting challenges significantly.  The project, costing nearly Rs 2,000 crore, is expected to be completed in four years.

news.title: South Delhi building collapse: MCD seals adjoining building, flags G+4 structure in resettlement colony
news.para: In Satya Niketan, a tragic incident occurred as a five-storey building crumbled, resulting in the deaths of at least three students. Witnesses attribute the disaster to ongoing repair work and excessive water accumulation in the basement. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has responded by evacuating and securing a neighboring structure. Efforts continue as rescue teams work tirelessly to locate any trapped individuals within the nearly 30-year-old building.

news.title: Delhi: Building was being repaired due to waterlogging in basement, say Satya Niketan residents
news.para: A tragic incident unfolded in Satya Niketan as a five-storey building collapsed, trapping several students inside. Locals pointed fingers at inadequate drainage and rampant construction practices for the catastrophe. Accusations of negligence towards building owners and civic agencies surfaced, highlighting public outrage. As rescue teams work tirelessly, the event raises serious questions about safety standards and maintenance protocols in the vicinity.

news.title: Delhi: Signature view residents seek time-bound redevelopment
news.para: Residents of Signature View Apartments are preparing to approach the Delhi High Court very soon to enforce a previous court order for the demolition and rebuilding of their unsafe flats. Having vacated their homes nearly a year ago, they are now advocating for a definitive timeline for the construction of their residences. This move is aimed at ensuring adherence to court directives and pushing for actual progress in the matter.

news.title: Odisha RERA safety net skips victims of fake property ads on social media
news.para: Akshay Moharana, a software professional, nearly lost one lakh rupees due to a deceitful social media advertisement, while teacher Rajesh Babu fell into the trap and paid an advance for a plot after encountering a similar misleading ad. These incidents highlight a glaring consumer protection failure for investors. Unregistered online sellers reveal that RERA relief is often inaccessible.

news.title: Haryana RERA orders Ocus Skyscrapers Realty to pay 10.8% interest to homebuyer for delayed flat handover
news.para: The Haryana Rera has mandated that Ocus Skyscrapers Realty pay a substantial 10.8% interest for the delay in delivering possession to Archana Dubey. Scheduled for December 2018, the possession was only provided in July 2019, thereby breaching the agreement. Additionally, the authority requested that the developer finalize the conveyance deed promptly, while dismissing other serious allegations against them.

news.title: NCLT approves Shree Naman's ₹1,800 crore bid for Gstaad, Neo Hotels
news.para: The bankruptcy court in Mumbai has greenlit Shree Naman Developers' ambitious acquisition valued at ₹1,800 crore for two hotel establishments. This comprehensive plan allocates ₹1,611 crore to Gstaad Hotels and ₹189 crore to Neo Capricorn Plaza, significantly surpassing the total admitted liabilities of around ₹1,227 crore. The resolution aims to maintain the corporate entities as ongoing operations, reflecting Shree Naman Developers' robust strategy of acquiring distressed businesses via insolvency procedures.

news.title: Bihar ministers discuss new building bylaws for faster approvals
news.para: Bihar's upcoming Building Bylaws for 2026 seek to streamline the approval processes. A high-level group of ministers has scrutinized the draft regulations. This initiative aims to enhance transparency and promote construction throughout the state, supporting critical infrastructure development and boosting economic activities. Ultimately, these proposed bylaws align with the ambitious vision for a progressive Bihar.

news.title: Pimpri Chinchwad civic body likely to record low property tax collection compared to previous two years
news.para: The Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation predicts a dip in property tax revenues for the upcoming fiscal year. In a bid to enhance collection rates, heightened enforcement actions have been initiated. Political candidates and residents in red zones are responding positively to various incentives offered. To further the recovery process, over eighty non-residential properties have been seized by tax authorities, and water supply cut-offs are being implemented.

news.title: Chandigarh scraps mandatory no-dues certificate for leasehold property sale
news.para: The Chandigarh administration has eliminated the requirement for a no-dues certificate, streamlining the process of selling leasehold properties in the Union Territory. This amendment, championed by the Property Consultants Association Chandigarh, significantly accelerates real estate transactions. As a result, buyers, sellers, and consultants can expect a smoother experience with reduced administrative hold-ups.

news.title: CBI books Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra, others over alleged ₹1,322 crore LICHFL loan loss
news.para: Subhash Chandra, along with eight others, is under scrutiny as the CBI has registered an FIR accusing them of inflating their net worth to secure loans fraudulently. This situation has led LIC Housing Finance to announce a staggering loss exceeding ₹1,322 crore. The Directorate of Enforcement will also step in with a money laundering investigation, and those accused can expect to be questioned soon about these dubious financial activities.

news.title: SC-appointed team surveys sites in Lucknow for land use violations
news.para: A Supreme Court team conducted a detailed survey of land-use regulations in Lucknow. They focused on properties in Aliganj flagged for regulatory breaches, while also investigating the responses by the Lucknow Development Authority. The inspections encompassed sites in Sarsawan, Gomti Nagar Extension, and Wellness City, with the results to be forwarded to the Supreme Court shortly for their consideration.

news.title: Over 180 MahaRERA recovery warrants worth ₹146.5 crore pending in Pune district; collector sets April deadline
news.para: Pune district collector Jitendra Dudi ordered revenue officials to execute all pending MahaRERA recovery warrants.  He stressed that homebuyers must receive their hard-earned money without further delay.  186 recovery warrant orders totaling Rs146.5 crore remained pending as of January 2026.  Officials will take coercive measures against defaulting developers to meet the April-end deadline.  The district's recovery data will be uploaded to the collectorate website for public transparency.

news.title: Mumbai: For flouting pollution norms, BMC to revoke builders’ project permission
news.para: Responding to escalating air quality concerns, the BMC has implemented tough penalties for construction sites that fail to adopt effective air pollution mitigation strategies. Architects and developers could face suspension of licenses or revocation of development permissions if they do not comply. Additionally, a 100% penalty will be imposed on applicable premium rates for any unauthorized work conducted after a stop-work notice.

news.title: NGT orders Pune builder to pay ₹7.36 crore compensation for construction without environmental clearance
news.para: The National Green Tribunal mandated a Pune developer to pay Rs 7.36 crore as compensation for engaging in construction activities without obtaining the necessary Environmental Clearance. The tribunal distinguished between two project phases for evaluation purposes. Consequently, authorities will assess damages and enforce penalties based on the violation framework, with the compensation allocated for environmental enhancement in the impacted area.

news.title: Labour department gets 10 days to verify crèche compliance at Noida construction sites
news.para: In an effort to protect workers, the district administration has allowed the labour department ten days to conduct inspections of construction sites. This initiative follows a mandate for crèche facilities at any site with fifty or more employees, ensuring that these spaces are clean, safe, and easily reachable. The directive comes in wake of a disturbing rape-murder incident, with heavy penalties for non-compliant developers looming on the horizon.
